title: [Mouse Without Borders] Rejected SettingsSync server: untrusted-signature / Settings.exe and MWB binaries are signed with different certificates (v0.101.2652.0+)

judgment.rationale: The comments extend the defect beyond GitHub per-user installation to Microsoft Store and the reciprocal IPC direction. Preserve the verification boundary and align the released peer binaries with the accepted signer policy. #51620 and #51077 are tracking/corroborating context, not independent fixes. Preserve primary tracking in #50795. Do not present cross-release file replacement as an approved correction or weaken signer/version checks.
evidence: The original 0.101.2652.0 report records repeated SettingsSync rejection in both service modes and different Microsoft signer certificates for Settings and MWB executables.
A commenter reconfirmed the same error on 0.102.3001, with the same two certificates assigned to opposite executables, and reported downgrade to 0.101.2362.0 restored pairing.
A later Store-install report on 0.102.0→0.102.3001 records reciprocal MWB-side rejection of Settings IPC and describes incomplete workarounds.
Current NamedPipePeerVerification source requires same trusted signer identity for signed peers and compares signer certificate bytes.

A new commenter reports that replacing the three MWB launcher executables with files from another release restored pairing on two x64 machine-wide installations: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/51567#issuecomment-6482766769

This is an unofficial mixed-version workaround reported by one commenter, not independently validated, a shipped fix, or evidence covering other architectures/install scopes. A Settings executable swap reportedly caused a runner version mismatch.
The maintainer renamed the primary issue to identify the SettingsSync signer-certificate mismatch and pinned it. The late timeline adds no new code repair or additional reporter evidence.
judgment.recommended_action: Continue the trust-preserving release-signing consistency correction in #50795; validate complete packages rather than endorsing mixed-version replacement.

fix_assessment.rationale: The certificate mismatch and rejection condition are demonstrated. Align release signing with the existing peer policy; the evidence does not justify broadening trust to a subject-name-only comparison.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep Settings and MWB peers on a signer accepted by the existing policy
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The shipped Settings and MWB binaries are Microsoft-signed with different leaf certificates, while SettingsSync requires the trusted peer signer certificates to match exactly.
plan: Trace release signing assignment for the affected Settings and MWB binaries and align the released peer binaries with the existing accepted-signer policy.
Retain rejection of untrusted peers; do not replace trusted-signer validation with a broad publisher-name comparison solely to accommodate the release mismatch.
verification: For each affected package, verify both signatures and the existing signer comparison in both service modes; confirm New key and SettingsSync succeed without the rejection.

Use intact signed release packages for x64/ARM64 and each install scope; verify Settings-to-MWB and runner-to-Settings communication, service modes and normal update/repair. The unofficial two-machine result is not this validation.

confidence.rationale: The exact comparison and affected-release signer identities directly account for the rejection; only the specific signing-pipeline correction remains to be chosen.
